chapters.title: The Waters of Meribah
chapters.html:
Numbers 20

Miriam Dies

1The sons of Israel, the whole congregation, came into the wilderness of Zin in the first month, and the people stayed in Kadesh. Miriam died there and was buried there.

Water from the Rock

2There was no water for the congregation, and they gathered against Moses and against Aaron.

3The people quarreled with Moses and said, "If only we had died when our brothers died before the LORD!

4Why have you brought the assembly of the LORD into this wilderness, for us and our livestock to die here?

5Why did you bring us up out of Egypt, to bring us to this terrible place? It is no place for grain, or figs, or vines, or pomegranates, and there is no water to drink."

6Moses and Aaron went from the assembly to the entrance of the tent of meeting and fell on their faces, and the glory of the LORD appeared to them.

7The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

8"Take the staff, and gather the congregation, you and Aaron your brother, and speak to the rock before their eyes, and it will give its water. So you will bring water out of the rock for them and give the congregation and their livestock drink."

9So Moses took the staff from before the LORD, as He had commanded him.

10Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly in front of the rock, and he said to them, "Listen now, you rebels: must we bring water out of this rock for you?"

11Moses raised his hand and struck the rock with his staff twice, and much water came out, and the congregation and their livestock drank.

12The LORD said to Moses and to Aaron, "Because you did not trust Me, to show Me holy before the eyes of the sons of Israel, therefore you shall not bring this assembly into the land that I have given them."

13These are the waters of Meribah, where the sons of Israel quarreled with the LORD, and He showed Himself holy among them.

Edom Refuses

14Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom: "Thus says your brother Israel: You know all the hardship that has come on us —

15how our fathers went down to Egypt, and we lived in Egypt many days, and the Egyptians treated us and our fathers badly.

16When we cried out to the LORD, He heard our voice and sent a messenger and brought us out of Egypt. Here we are in Kadesh, a town at the edge of your border.

17Please let us pass through your land. We will not pass through field or vineyard, or drink water from a well. We will go by the King's Highway. We will not turn aside to the right or to the left until we have passed through your border."

18Edom said to him, "You shall not pass through me, or I will come out against you with the sword."

19The sons of Israel said to him, "We will go up by the highway, and if we drink your water, I and my livestock, I will pay for it. It is nothing — let me only pass through on foot."

20He said, "You shall not pass through." Edom came out against them with a large army and a strong hand.

21So Edom refused to let Israel pass through his border, and Israel turned away from him.

Aaron Dies

22They set out from Kadesh, and the sons of Israel, the whole congregation, came to Mount Hor.

23The LORD said to Moses and to Aaron at Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom,

24"Aaron shall be gathered to his people, for he shall not enter the land that I have given to the sons of Israel, because you rebelled against My command at the waters of Meribah.

25Take Aaron and Eleazar his son and bring them up Mount Hor.

26Strip Aaron of his garments and put them on Eleazar his son. Aaron shall be gathered to his people and die there."

27Moses did as the LORD commanded. They went up Mount Hor before the eyes of the whole congregation.

28Moses stripped Aaron of his garments and put them on Eleazar his son, and Aaron died there on the top of the mountain. Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.

29When the whole congregation saw that Aaron had died, all the house of Israel wept for Aaron thirty days.

Notes

  • v1 "the first month" — the text gives no year. The next date in Numbers puts Aaron's death on Mount Hor in the fortieth year (33:38), so the story has passed over almost the whole forty years of 14:33 in silence, from the scouts to this month. Miriam's death gets seven words, and no mourning is recorded, as it is for Aaron (v29).

  • vv2–13 the rock at Meribah, a second time — at Horeb, near the start of the journey, the LORD told Moses to strike the rock (Exodus 17:6), and that place was also named Meribah, for the people's quarreling (Exodus 17:7). Here he is told to take the staff and speak to the rock (v8). He strikes it, twice.

  • v10 "you rebels" — ha-morim, from the root of benei meri, the rebels of 17:10, for whom Aaron's staff was kept as a sign. Moses takes the staff from that place (v9) and uses the word the LORD used. In v24 the same verb comes back on Moses and Aaron: you rebelled against My command.

  • v10 "must we bring water… for you?" — we, not the LORD. The text names no single fault, and v12 names only one: you did not trust Me, to show Me holy. Psalm 106:32–33 says of this place that it went badly for Moses because of them, for they rebelled against his spirit, and he spoke rashly with his lips. The rebels' verb there is himru, the root of morim.

  • v13 "He showed Himself holy among them" — va-yiqqadesh, from qadosh, holy, the root of the place name Kadesh (v1). At Holy-place the LORD showed Himself holy, even though His two servants had not shown Him so (v12).

  • v14 "your brother Israel" — Edom is Esau, and Israel is Jacob (Genesis 36:1; 32:28). Moses' message opens on the brothers of Genesis, who parted in peace (Genesis 33).

  • v16 "sent a messenger" — mal'akh, the same word as the messengers Moses sends to Edom in v14. It is also the word for the angel of God who went before Israel's camp at the sea (Exodus 14:19).

  • v20 "with a large army and a strong hand" — be-yad chazakah, the phrase of the LORD's power against Pharaoh (Exodus 6:1). Edom turns it against Israel, and Israel turns away (v21).

  • vv26–28 Aaron's garments on Eleazar — the holy garments of Aaron shall belong to his sons after him, to be anointed in them (Exodus 29:29). The office passes to Eleazar on the mountain before Aaron dies, and the high priest dies out of his vestments. The Greek says in v29 that Aaron was released, apelythē, where the Hebrew has died.

chapters.title: The Bronze Serpent
chapters.html:
Numbers 21

Hormah

1The Canaanite, the king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that Israel was coming by the road to Atharim. He fought against Israel and took some of them captive.

2Israel made a vow to the LORD and said, "If You will indeed give this people into my hand, I will devote their towns to destruction."

3The LORD listened to the voice of Israel and gave up the Canaanites, and they devoted them and their towns to destruction. So the name of the place was called Hormah.

The Bronze Serpent

4They set out from Mount Hor by the way of the Sea of Reeds, to go around the land of Edom, and the people grew impatient on the way.

5The people spoke against God and against Moses: "Why have you brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? There is no bread and no water, and we are sick of this miserable bread."

6So the LORD sent the fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people, and many people of Israel died.

7The people came to Moses and said, "We have sinned, because we have spoken against the LORD and against you. Pray to the LORD, so that He takes the serpents away from us." So Moses prayed for the people.

8The LORD said to Moses, "Make a fiery serpent and set it on a pole. Everyone who is bitten, when he sees it, shall live."

9So Moses made a bronze serpent and set it on the pole. Whenever a serpent bit a man, he would look to the bronze serpent and live.

The Journey to Moab

10The sons of Israel set out and camped at Oboth.

11They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, in the wilderness facing Moab, toward the sunrise.

12From there they set out and camped in the valley of Zered.

13From there they set out and camped on the other side of the Arnon, which is in the wilderness that extends from the border of the Amorites. The Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.

14That is why it is said in the Book of the Wars of the LORD:
"Waheb in Suphah,
and the valleys of the Arnon,

15and the slope of the valleys
that turns toward the dwelling of Ar
and leans on the border of Moab."

16From there they went on to Beer. That is the well where the LORD said to Moses, "Gather the people, and I will give them water."

17Then Israel sang this song:
"Spring up, O well! Sing to it —

18the well the princes dug,
the nobles of the people carved it out,
with the ruler's rod, with their staffs."
From the wilderness they went on to Mattanah,

19from Mattanah to Nahaliel, from Nahaliel to Bamoth,

20and from Bamoth to the valley in the country of Moab, at the top of Pisgah, which looks down on the wasteland.

Sihon and Og

21Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, saying,

22"Let me pass through your land. We will not turn aside into field or vineyard. We will not drink water from a well. We will go by the King's Highway until we have passed through your border."

23But Sihon would not let Israel pass through his border. Sihon gathered all his people and went out against Israel into the wilderness, and came to Jahaz and fought against Israel.

24Israel struck him with the sword and took possession of his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the Ammonites, for the border of the Ammonites was strong.

25Israel took all these towns, and Israel lived in all the towns of the Amorites, in Heshbon and all its villages.

26For Heshbon was the town of Sihon king of the Amorites. He had fought against the former king of Moab and taken all his land out of his hand, as far as the Arnon.

27That is why the singers of sayings say:
"Come to Heshbon, let it be built!
Let the town of Sihon be set up!

28For fire went out from Heshbon,
a flame from the town of Sihon.
It consumed Ar of Moab,
the lords of the heights of the Arnon.

29Woe to you, Moab!
You are lost, people of Chemosh!
He has given up his sons as fugitives,
and his daughters into captivity,
to Sihon king of the Amorites.

30We shot at them; Heshbon is lost, as far as Dibon.
We laid waste as far as Nophah,
which reaches to Medeba."

31So Israel lived in the land of the Amorites.

32Moses sent men to scout out Jazer, and they took its villages and drove out the Amorites who were there.

33Then they turned and went up by the road to Bashan, and Og king of Bashan came out against them, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.

34The LORD said to Moses, "Do not be afraid of him, for I have given him into your hand, with all his people and his land. You shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon."

35So they struck him and his sons and all his people, until no survivor was left to him, and they took possession of his land.

Notes

  • v1 "the road to Atharim" — derekh ha-atarim, which the Greek takes as a place name, Atharin. Read with one letter's difference it would be the road of the scouts, ha-tarim, the word for the men who scouted the land (13:2, 13:25), and that is how some English versions render it.

  • v3 "Hormah" — from charam, devote to destruction, the verb of vv2 and 3: to hand over to the LORD by destroying, with nothing kept as plunder. It is the place where Israel, going up against the LORD's word, was beaten as far as Hormah (14:45). Now, going up with a vow to the LORD, they win there.

  • v6 "the fiery serpents" — ha-nechashim ha-serafim, from saraf, to burn, most likely for the burning of the bite. The same word, serafim, names the six-winged beings above the LORD's throne in Isaiah 6:2. The Greek has the deadly serpents.

  • vv8–9 "a fiery serpent… a bronze serpent… on the pole" — nechash nechoshet, a serpent of bronze, two words from the same three letters. The pole is nes, the rallying signal of Exodus 17:15, The LORD Is My Banner. The people are healed by looking at an image of what bit them. Hezekiah later broke it in pieces, for until those days the sons of Israel had been burning incense to it, and it was called Nehushtan (2 Kings 18:4). Jesus says, as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up (John 3:14).

  • vv14–15 the Book of the Wars of the LORD — a book quoted here and nowhere else, and lost. The quotation begins in the middle of a sentence, et Vahev be-Sufah, with an object marker and no verb, and Waheb and Suphah appear nowhere else. They are probably places. The Greek reads a verb into it: he set Zoob on fire.

  • vv17–18 the song of the well — Beer means well, and Mattanah, the next stop, means gift, from natan, the verb of the LORD's promise at the well: I will give them water (v16).

  • v27 "the singers of sayings" — ha-moshlim, those who speak a mashal, a saying, proverb or taunt song. The same word names Balaam's oracles in the next chapters (23:7). The song of Heshbon is used again in Jeremiah, against Moab: fire went out from Heshbon… Woe to you, Moab! The people of Chemosh are lost (Jeremiah 48:45–46).

  • v30 "We laid waste as far as Nophah, which reaches to Medeba" — the Hebrew scribes put a dot over one letter of asher, which, marking it as doubtful. Without that letter the word is esh, fire, and the Greek reads it so, with nashim, women, for we laid waste (the same consonants): and the women kindled fire on Moab. The text here follows the Hebrew as written.

  • v32 "drove out" — the written text has vayyirash, took possession, and the reading tradition has vayyoresh, drove out. The text follows the reading.

From there they set out and camped in the valley of Zered.

the well the princes dug, the nobles of the people carved it out, with the ruler's rod, with their staffs." From the wilderness they went on to Mattanah,
from Mattanah to Nahaliel, from Nahaliel to Bamoth,

Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, saying,
"Let me pass through your land. We will not turn aside into field or vineyard. We will not drink water from a well. We will go by the King's Highway until we have passed through your border."

Israel struck him with the sword and took possession of his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the Ammonites, for the border of the Ammonites was strong.
Israel took all these towns, and Israel lived in all the towns of the Amorites, in Heshbon and all its villages.
For Heshbon was the town of Sihon king of the Amorites. He had fought against the former king of Moab and taken all his land out of his hand, as far as the Arnon.
That is why the singers of sayings say: "Come to Heshbon, let it be built! Let the town of Sihon be set up!
For fire went out from Heshbon, a flame from the town of Sihon. It consumed Ar of Moab, the lords of the heights of the Arnon.
Woe to you, Moab! You are lost, people of Chemosh! He has given up his sons as fugitives, and his daughters into captivity, to Sihon king of the Amorites.
We shot at them; Heshbon is lost, as far as Dibon. We laid waste as far as Nophah, which reaches to Medeba."
So Israel lived in the land of the Amorites.
Moses sent men to scout out Jazer, and they took its villages and drove out the Amorites who were there.
Then they turned and went up by the road to Bashan, and Og king of Bashan came out against them, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.

The LORD said to Moses, "Do not be afraid of him, for I have given him into your hand, with all his people and his land. You shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon."

chapters.title: Balaam and the Donkey
chapters.html:
Numbers 22

Balak Sends for Balaam

1The sons of Israel set out and camped in the plains of Moab, across the Jordan from Jericho.

2Balak son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites.

3Moab was very afraid of the people, because they were many. Moab dreaded the sons of Israel.

4Moab said to the elders of Midian, "Now this company will lick up everything around us, as the ox licks up the green of the field." Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time.

5He sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor at Pethor, which is by the River, in the land of the sons of his people, to call him, saying, "Here — a people has come out of Egypt. Here — they have covered the eye of the land, and they are living opposite me.

6And now please come and curse this people for me, for they are too mighty for me. Perhaps I will be able to strike them and drive them out of the land. For I know that whoever you bless is blessed, and whoever you curse is cursed."

7The elders of Moab and the elders of Midian went with the fees for soothsaying in their hand. They came to Balaam and spoke Balak's words to him.

8He said to them, "Spend the night here, and I will bring you back word, as the LORD speaks to me." So the chiefs of Moab stayed with Balaam.

9God came to Balaam and said, "Who are these men with you?"

10Balaam said to God, "Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, has sent to me:

11'Here — the people that has come out of Egypt has covered the eye of the land. Now come, put a curse on them for me. Perhaps I will be able to fight against them and drive them out.'"

12God said to Balaam, "You shall not go with them. You shall not curse the people, for they are blessed."

13Balaam rose in the morning and said to Balak's chiefs, "Go to your own land, for the LORD has refused to let me go with you."

14So the chiefs of Moab rose and went to Balak and said, "Balaam refused to come with us."

The Second Embassy

15Balak sent chiefs again, more of them and more honored than these.

16They came to Balaam and said to him, "Thus says Balak son of Zippor: Please let nothing keep you from coming to me,

17for I will honor you greatly, and whatever you tell me I will do. Please come, put a curse on this people for me."

18Balaam answered and said to Balak's servants, "If Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the command of the LORD my God, to do anything small or great.

19And now please stay here tonight, you also, so that I may know what more the LORD will say to me."

20God came to Balaam at night and said to him, "If the men have come to call you, rise, go with them. But you shall do only what I tell you."

21So Balaam rose in the morning and saddled his donkey and went with the chiefs of Moab.

The Donkey

22But God's anger burned because he was going, and the angel of the LORD took his stand in the road as an adversary against him. He was riding on his donkey, and his two young men were with him.

23The donkey saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with his sword drawn in his hand, and the donkey turned off the road and went into the field. Balaam struck the donkey to turn her back onto the road.

24Then the angel of the LORD stood in a narrow path between the vineyards, with a wall on this side and a wall on that side.

25The donkey saw the angel of the LORD and pressed herself against the wall, and pressed Balaam's foot against the wall, and he struck her again.

26The angel of the LORD went on ahead and stood in a narrow place where there was no way to turn to the right or to the left.

27The donkey saw the angel of the LORD and lay down under Balaam. Balaam's anger burned, and he struck the donkey with his stick.

28The LORD opened the donkey's mouth, and she said to Balaam, "What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?"

29Balaam said to the donkey, "Because you have made a fool of me! If only there were a sword in my hand, I would kill you now."

30The donkey said to Balaam, "Am I not your donkey, whom you have ridden all your life to this day? Have I ever been in the habit of doing this to you?" He said, "No."

31Then the LORD uncovered Balaam's eyes, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with his sword drawn in his hand. He bowed and fell on his face.

32The angel of the LORD said to him, "Why have you struck your donkey these three times? Here — I have come out as an adversary, because your way is headlong before me.

33The donkey saw me and turned aside before me these three times. If she had not turned aside from me, I would surely have killed you by now, and let her live."

34Balaam said to the angel of the LORD, "I have sinned, for I did not know that you were standing in the road against me. And now, if it is displeasing to you, I will go back."

35The angel of the LORD said to Balaam, "Go with the men, but you shall speak only the word that I speak to you." So Balaam went with the chiefs of Balak.

Balak Meets Balaam

36When Balak heard that Balaam had come, he went out to meet him at the town of Moab on the border of the Arnon, at the edge of the border.

37Balak said to Balaam, "Did I not send to you to call you? Why did you not come to me? Am I really not able to honor you?"

38Balaam said to Balak, "Here — I have come to you. Now, am I able to speak anything at all? I shall speak the word that God puts in my mouth."

39Balaam went with Balak, and they came to Kiriath-huzoth.

40Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep, and sent some to Balaam and to the chiefs who were with him.

41And it came to pass in the morning that Balak took Balaam and brought him up to Bamoth-baal, and from there he saw the edge of the people.

Notes

  • v3 "Moab dreaded the sons of Israel" — va-yaqots… mipnei benei Yisra'el, the words of Exodus 1:12, where Egypt dreaded the sons of Israel because they kept multiplying. The king of Moab opens this story where Pharaoh opened Exodus.

  • v5 "they have covered the eye of the land" — kissah et ein ha-arets, the phrase of the locusts in Exodus 10:5. Balak sees Israel as a swarm, and v4 says it plainly: they will lick up everything around us.

  • v5 "the land of the sons of his people" — that is, Balaam's own country. The Latin reads the land of the sons of Ammon, a difference of one letter (ammo, his people; Ammon). The River, with no name, is the Euphrates, as in Genesis 31:21.

  • vv6, 11 two words for curse — Balak's message says arah, from arar, the word of Genesis 12:3, the one who treats you lightly I will curse. When Balaam repeats the message to God he uses qavah, from qavav, a rarer word for cursing, and Balak uses it himself in v17. Balak's boast, whoever you bless is blessed, and whoever you curse is cursed, turns around the blessing Isaac gave Jacob: Those who curse you, cursed; and those who bless you, blessed (Genesis 27:29).

  • v22 "as an adversary against him" — le-satan lo. Satan is the common noun for an opponent or accuser (see Genesis 26:21), and here it is the angel of the LORD who is Balaam's satan. The Greek has diaballein, to oppose, from which comes diabolos, the devil.

  • v28 "these three times" — shalosh regalim, literally three feet, the unusual phrase used for Israel's three pilgrim festivals (Exodus 23:14). It comes three times in the chapter (vv28, 32, 33). Balak will say these three times to Balaam in 24:10, after Balaam has blessed Israel three times instead of cursing it.

  • v29 "you have made a fool of me" — hit'allalt bi, the verb the LORD uses of what He did to Egypt (Exodus 10:2). The seer who sees nothing is outseen by his donkey, three times.

  • v32 "your way is headlong" — yarat, a rare verb. In its one other clear use, Job says God throws me into the hands of the wicked (Job 16:11). The meaning here is uncertain; reckless, perverse and headlong all fit the context. The Greek has your way is not seemly before me.

  • v35 "only the word that I speak to you" — the command of v20, repeated with speak where v20 had do. The difference is what Balaam now knows: the road is open to him only on those terms. The New Testament remembers him for the fees of v7, Balaam son of Beor, who loved the wages of wrongdoing, rebuked by a speechless beast speaking with a man's voice (2 Peter 2:15–16).

chapters.title: Balaam's First Two Sayings
chapters.html:
Numbers 23

The First Saying

1Balaam said to Balak, "Build me seven altars here, and prepare me seven bulls and seven rams here."

2Balak did as Balaam had said, and Balak and Balaam offered a bull and a ram on each altar.

3Balaam said to Balak, "Stand beside your burnt offering, and I will go. Perhaps the LORD will come to meet me, and whatever He shows me I will tell you." Then he went to a bare height.

4God met Balaam, and Balaam said to Him, "I have set up the seven altars, and I have offered a bull and a ram on each altar."

5The LORD put a word in Balaam's mouth and said, "Go back to Balak, and this is what you shall say."

6So he went back to him, and here — he was standing beside his burnt offering, he and all the chiefs of Moab.

7He took up his saying and said:
"From Aram Balak has brought me,
the king of Moab from the mountains of the east:
'Come, curse Jacob for me,
come, denounce Israel!'

8How can I put a curse on one God has not cursed?
How can I denounce one the LORD has not denounced?

9For from the top of the rocks I see him,
from the hills I watch him.
Here is a people that lives alone,
and does not count itself among the nations.

10Who can count the dust of Jacob,
or number the fourth part of Israel?
Let me die the death of the upright,
and let my end be like his!"

11Balak said to Balaam, "What have you done to me? I took you to curse my enemies, and here — you have done nothing but bless them!"

12He answered and said, "Must I not take care to speak what the LORD puts in my mouth?"

The Second Saying

13Balak said to him, "Please come with me to another place, where you will see them. You will see only the edge of them; you will not see all of them. Curse them for me from there."

14So he took him to the field of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah, and built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.

15Balaam said to Balak, "Stand here beside your burnt offering, while I meet the LORD over there."

16The LORD met Balaam and put a word in his mouth, and said, "Go back to Balak, and this is what you shall say."

17He came to him, and here — he was standing beside his burnt offering, with the chiefs of Moab. Balak said to him, "What has the LORD spoken?"

18He took up his saying and said:
"Rise, Balak, and hear;
listen to me, son of Zippor.

19God is not a man, that He should lie,
or a son of man, that He should change His mind.
Has He said, and will He not do it?
Has He spoken, and will He not make it stand?

20Here — I have received a command to bless.
He has blessed, and I cannot turn it back.

21He has not looked on wrongdoing in Jacob,
or seen trouble in Israel.
The LORD his God is with him,
and the shout of a king is among them.

22God brings them out of Egypt;
he has the horns of the wild ox.

23For there is no divining in Jacob,
no soothsaying in Israel.
Now it shall be said of Jacob and of Israel,
'What God has done!'

24Here is a people that rises like a lioness,
and lifts itself up like a lion.
It does not lie down until it eats the prey
and drinks the blood of the slain."

25Balak said to Balaam, "Do not curse them at all, and do not bless them at all!"

26Balaam answered and said to Balak, "Did I not tell you, 'Everything the LORD speaks, that I must do'?"

To Peor

27Balak said to Balaam, "Please come, I will take you to another place. Perhaps it will be right in the eyes of God that you curse them for me from there."

28So Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, which looks down on the wasteland.

29Balaam said to Balak, "Build me seven altars here, and prepare me seven bulls and seven rams here."

30Balak did as Balaam had said, and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.

Notes

  • v3 "a bare height" — shefi, a word of uncertain meaning, used of the bare hills in Isaiah 41:18 and Jeremiah 3:2. The Greek reads it differently: Balaam went to inquire of God, and went straight.

  • vv4, 16 "God met Balaam" — va-yiqqar, from qarah, to happen upon, to meet by chance. Balaam expected to go out and find the LORD (v3). Each time, the text says God came to him.

  • v7 "his saying" — meshalo, his mashal, the word for the song of Heshbon's singers (21:27): a saying, a proverb, a poem with a point. The Greek has parabolē, parable. The saying is poetry, and the story around it is prose.

  • vv7–8 "curse… denounce" — three words for cursing in two verses. Balak asked for arah and za'amah, curse and denounce, and the answer uses qavav, the word of 22:11, with za'am, the word for God's indignation: How can I… whom the LORD has not denounced?

  • v9 "a people that lives alone" — am le-vadad yishkon. Moses' blessing ends on the same two words, shakhan, live, and badad, alone: Israel lives in safety, alone (Deuteronomy 33:28). Does not count itself among the nations is lo yitchashav, it does not reckon itself one of them.

  • v10 "the dust of Jacob… the fourth part of Israel" — the dust is the promise of Genesis 13:16 and 28:14, your seed shall be as the dust of the earth, which if a man could count, could be counted. Rova is usually taken as a fourth part, but the word is uncertain here. The Greek has the clans of Israel.

  • v10 "let me die the death of the upright" — yesharim. Balaam wishes for Israel's end, and the text records his: he is killed with the sword among the kings of Midian (31:8).

  • v19 "God is not a man, that He should lie" — Samuel says the same of God when he tells Saul the kingdom has been torn from him: He is not a man, that He should change His mind (1 Samuel 15:29).

  • v22 "the horns of the wild ox" — ke-to'afot re'em. Re'em is the wild ox, and to'afot is uncertain: horns, peaks, or strength. The Greek renders re'em with monokerōs, one-horn, and from there the older English versions have unicorn.

  • v23 "no divining in Jacob" — lo nachash be-Ya'aqov. The preposition be- means both in and against: there is no divining in Jacob, or no divining will work against Jacob. Both fit the story, where a diviner has been hired against Israel. Nachash is the practice forbidden in Leviticus 19:26, and qesem is what the elders of Moab brought fees for (22:7).

chapters.title: A Star out of Jacob
chapters.html:
Numbers 24

The Third Saying

1When Balaam saw that it pleased the LORD to bless Israel, he did not go, as at the other times, to look for divinings, but set his face toward the wilderness.

2Balaam lifted up his eyes and saw Israel camping tribe by tribe, and the Spirit of God came on him.

3He took up his saying and said:
"The word of Balaam son of Beor,
the word of the man whose eye is opened,

4the word of one who hears the sayings of God,
who sees the vision of the Almighty,
falling down, with his eyes uncovered:

5How good are your tents, O Jacob,
your dwellings, O Israel!

6Like valleys they stretch out,
like gardens beside a river,
like aloes that the LORD has planted,
like cedars beside the waters.

7Water shall flow from his buckets,
and his seed shall be in many waters.
His king shall be higher than Agag,
and his kingdom shall be lifted up.

8God brings him out of Egypt;
he has the horns of the wild ox.
He shall eat up the nations, his foes,
and crush their bones,
and strike them through with his arrows.

9He crouched, he lay down like a lion,
and like a lioness — who will rouse him?
Blessed are those who bless you,
and cursed are those who curse you."

10Balak's anger burned against Balaam, and he struck his hands together. Balak said to Balaam, "I called you to put a curse on my enemies, and here — you have done nothing but bless them these three times!

11And now flee to your own place. I said I would honor you greatly, but here — the LORD has kept you back from honor."

12Balaam said to Balak, "Did I not tell your messengers whom you sent to me,

13'If Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the command of the LORD, to do good or bad from my own heart. What the LORD speaks, that I will speak'?

14And now I am going to my people. Come, I will tell you what this people will do to your people in the end of days."

The Fourth Saying

15He took up his saying and said:
"The word of Balaam son of Beor,
the word of the man whose eye is opened,

16the word of one who hears the sayings of God,
and knows what the Most High knows,
who sees the vision of the Almighty,
falling down, with his eyes uncovered:

17I see him, but not now;
I watch him, but not near.
A star shall march out of Jacob,
and a staff shall rise out of Israel.
It shall crush the brow of Moab
and tear down all the sons of Sheth.

18Edom shall be a possession,
Seir, his enemies, shall be a possession,
while Israel does valiantly.

19One from Jacob shall rule,
and destroy what survives of the city."

The Last Sayings

20He looked on Amalek, and took up his saying and said:
"Amalek was first among the nations,
but his end is destruction."

21He looked on the Kenite, and took up his saying and said:
"Enduring is your dwelling place,
and your nest is set in the rock.

22Yet Kain shall be burned.
How long? Asshur will take you captive."

23He took up his saying and said:
"Alas, who shall live when God does this?

24Ships shall come from the coast of Kittim,
and they shall afflict Asshur and afflict Eber,
and he too shall come to destruction."

25Then Balaam rose and went back to his place, and Balak also went his way.

Notes

  • v1 "to look for divinings" — li-qrat nechashim, to meet divinings, the nachash that 23:23 said was not in Jacob. The two earlier sayings began with Balaam going off to meet the LORD (23:3, 23:15). This time he goes nowhere. He looks at Israel, and the Spirit of God came on him (v2).

  • vv3, 15 "the word of Balaam" — ne'um, the word that marks a prophet's utterance, almost always the word of the LORD (ne'um YHWH). Here Balaam uses it of himself.

  • vv3, 15 "whose eye is opened" — shetum ha-ayin. The verb is found only here, and it has been read both ways: opened or shut. Opened fits v4, with his eyes uncovered, the words of 22:31, where the LORD uncovered Balaam's eyes. The Greek has who sees truly.

  • v4 "the Almighty" — Shaddai, the name God gave Himself to Abraham as God Almighty (Genesis 17:1). This is its first appearance in Numbers, and it comes from a foreign seer.

  • v6 "like aloes" — ka-ahalim, a fragrant tree, and a play on ohalekha, your tents, in v5. The Greek reads it as tents: like tents that the Lord pitched.

  • v7 "higher than Agag" — Agag is the name of the king of Amalek whom Saul spared (1 Samuel 15:8). The Greek has Gog, and in place of the buckets, a man shall come out of his seed and rule over many nations.

  • v9 "He crouched, he lay down like a lion" — Jacob's words over Judah in Genesis 49:9, almost exactly. Blessed are those who bless you, and cursed are those who curse you is Isaac's blessing of Jacob (Genesis 27:29). The seer hired to curse ends by quoting the fathers' blessings back over their sons.

  • v17 "a star… a staff" — kokhav and shevet. Shevet is the ruler's staff of Genesis 49:10, the staff shall not turn aside from Judah, and the word for tribe in v2. The brow of Moab… the sons of Sheth is quoted in Jeremiah's judgment on Moab: fire… consumed the brow of Moab, the crown of the sons of tumult (Jeremiah 48:45). Jeremiah has qodqod, crown, for qarqar, tear down, and sha'on, tumult, for Sheth. The Greek has a man shall rise out of Israel.

  • v21 "your nest is set in the rock" — qinnekha, your nest, sounds like Qayin, Kain, the Kenites' name (v22). Verse 22 is the most uncertain line in the chapter: ki im yihyeh le-va'er Qayin may be yet Kain shall be burned or Kain shall be for grazing. Asshur here may be the Assyrians, or the Asshurim, a tribe of Genesis 25:3.

  • v24 "ships… from Kittim" — tsim miyyad Kittim. Kittim is a people of the western sea, a son of Javan in Genesis 10:4. Daniel 11:30 uses the same words for the ships that come against the king of the north.

chapters.title: Baal of Peor
chapters.html:
Numbers 25

Yoked to Baal of Peor

1While Israel was staying at Shittim, the people began to prostitute themselves with the daughters of Moab.

2The women invited the people to the sacrifices of their gods, and the people ate and bowed down to their gods.

3So Israel yoked itself to Baal of Peor, and the anger of the LORD burned against Israel.

4The LORD said to Moses, "Take all the chiefs of the people and hang them up before the LORD in the sun, so that the fierce anger of the LORD may turn away from Israel."

5Moses said to the judges of Israel, "Each of you kill those of his men who have yoked themselves to Baal of Peor."

Phinehas

6And here — one of the sons of Israel came and brought a Midianite woman to his brothers, before the eyes of Moses and before the eyes of the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, while they were weeping at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

7When Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose from among the congregation and took a spear in his hand.

8He went after the man of Israel into the tent chamber and pierced both of them, the man of Israel and the woman, through her belly. So the plague was stopped from the sons of Israel.

9Those who died in the plague were twenty-four thousand.

10The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

11"Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has turned back My wrath from the sons of Israel, because he was jealous with My jealousy among them, so that I did not consume the sons of Israel in My jealousy.

12Therefore say: Here — I give him My covenant of peace.

13It shall be for him and for his offspring after him a covenant of lasting priesthood, because he was jealous for his God and made atonement for the sons of Israel."

14The name of the man of Israel who was struck down with the Midianite woman was Zimri son of Salu, chief of a fathers' house of the Simeonites.

15The name of the Midianite woman who was struck down was Cozbi daughter of Zur, who was head of the clans of a fathers' house in Midian.

Against Midian

16The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

17"Harass the Midianites and strike them,

18for they have harassed you with their tricks, the tricks they played on you in the matter of Peor, and in the matter of Cozbi, the daughter of a chief of Midian, their sister, who was struck down on the day of the plague over the matter of Peor."

Notes

  • v1 "prostitute themselves" — liznot, the word of 15:39 for going after one's own eyes. The women invite the men to their gods' sacrifices (v2), and the text does not separate the two. Balaam's part comes out later: these women, by Balaam's word, caused the sons of Israel to break faith with the LORD in the matter of Peor (31:16). The Revelation to John remembers him for it: Balaam, who taught Balak to put a stumbling block before the sons of Israel, to eat food sacrificed to idols and to practice sexual immorality (Revelation 2:14).

  • v3 "Israel yoked itself to Baal of Peor" — va-yitsamed, from tsemed, a yoke of oxen: harnessed to him. Baal means lord or owner, and Baal of Peor is the god named for Peor, the mountain where Balak had taken Balaam (23:28). Psalm 106:28 adds that they ate sacrifices of the dead.

  • v4 "hang them up… in the sun" — hoqa, a rare verb for a public execution: hanging, impaling or exposing the bodies. It is the verb used when the Gibeonites put seven of Saul's sons to death before the LORD (2 Samuel 21:6, 9). The Greek has make an example of them.

  • v8 "into the tent chamber… through her belly" — el ha-qubbah… el qovatah, two words that sound alike. Qubbah is a vaulted tent, found only here. The Greek has into the furnace and through her womb.

  • v9 "twenty-four thousand" — Paul, warning the Corinthians against sexual immorality, says twenty-three thousand fell in one day (1 Corinthians 10:8). The Hebrew and the Greek of Numbers both have twenty-four thousand.

  • v11 "he was jealous with My jealousy" — be-qan'o et qin'ati, the word of the jealous God of Exodus 20:5, a husband's jealousy for his wife. Phinehas feels what God feels, and so God does not have to act on it.

  • v12 "My covenant of peace" — beriti shalom. Malachi recalls it of Levi: My covenant was with him, life and peace (Malachi 2:5). The psalm says of Phinehas, it was counted to him as righteousness from generation to generation (Psalm 106:31), the words of Abraham's faith in Genesis 15:6.

  • v17 "Harass… for they have harassed you" — tsaror… tsorerim, the same verb, given back. Tricks is nekhel, twice in one verse: they tricked you with their tricks.

chapters.title: The Second Count
chapters.html:
Numbers 26

The Count on the Plains of Moab

1And it came to pass after the plague that the LORD said to Moses and to Eleazar son of Aaron the priest,

2"Take a count of the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, from twenty years old and up, by their fathers' houses, all in Israel who can go out to war."

3So Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke with them in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho, saying,

4"From twenty years old and up," as the LORD had commanded Moses. The sons of Israel who came out of the land of Egypt were these:

5Reuben, the firstborn of Israel. The sons of Reuben: of Hanoch, the clan of the Hanochites; of Pallu, the clan of the Palluites;

6of Hezron, the clan of the Hezronites; of Carmi, the clan of the Carmites.

7These are the clans of the Reubenites, and those counted of them were forty-three thousand seven hundred and thirty.

8The son of Pallu: Eliab.

9The sons of Eliab: Nemuel and Dathan and Abiram. These are the Dathan and Abiram, called to the congregation, who fought against Moses and Aaron in the company of Korah when they fought against the LORD,

10and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up together with Korah, when that company died, when the fire consumed two hundred and fifty men, and they became a warning sign.

11But the sons of Korah did not die.

12The sons of Simeon by their clans: of Nemuel, the clan of the Nemuelites; of Jamin, the clan of the Jaminites; of Jachin, the clan of the Jachinites;

13of Zerah, the clan of the Zerahites; of Shaul, the clan of the Shaulites.

14These are the clans of the Simeonites, twenty-two thousand two hundred.

15The sons of Gad by their clans: of Zephon, the clan of the Zephonites; of Haggi, the clan of the Haggites; of Shuni, the clan of the Shunites;

16of Ozni, the clan of the Oznites; of Eri, the clan of the Erites;

17of Arod, the clan of the Arodites; of Areli, the clan of the Arelites.

18These are the clans of the sons of Gad as they were counted, forty thousand five hundred.

19The sons of Judah were Er and Onan, and Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.

20The sons of Judah by their clans were: of Shelah, the clan of the Shelanites; of Perez, the clan of the Perezites; of Zerah, the clan of the Zerahites.

21The sons of Perez were: of Hezron, the clan of the Hezronites; of Hamul, the clan of the Hamulites.

22These are the clans of Judah as they were counted, seventy-six thousand five hundred.

23The sons of Issachar by their clans: of Tola, the clan of the Tolaites; of Puvah, the clan of the Punites;

24of Jashub, the clan of the Jashubites; of Shimron, the clan of the Shimronites.

25These are the clans of Issachar as they were counted, sixty-four thousand three hundred.

26The sons of Zebulun by their clans: of Sered, the clan of the Seredites; of Elon, the clan of the Elonites; of Jahleel, the clan of the Jahleelites.

27These are the clans of the Zebulunites as they were counted, sixty thousand five hundred.

28The sons of Joseph by their clans: Manasseh and Ephraim.

29The sons of Manasseh: of Machir, the clan of the Machirites. Machir fathered Gilead; of Gilead, the clan of the Gileadites.

30These are the sons of Gilead: of Iezer, the clan of the Iezerites; of Helek, the clan of the Helekites;

31of Asriel, the clan of the Asrielites; of Shechem, the clan of the Shechemites;

32of Shemida, the clan of the Shemidaites; of Hepher, the clan of the Hepherites.

33Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons, only daughters, and the names of the daughters of Zelophehad were Mahlah and Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah.

34These are the clans of Manasseh, and those counted of them were fifty-two thousand seven hundred.

35These are the sons of Ephraim by their clans: of Shuthelah, the clan of the Shuthelahites; of Becher, the clan of the Becherites; of Tahan, the clan of the Tahanites.

36These are the sons of Shuthelah: of Eran, the clan of the Eranites.

37These are the clans of the sons of Ephraim as they were counted, thirty-two thousand five hundred. These are the sons of Joseph by their clans.

38The sons of Benjamin by their clans: of Bela, the clan of the Belaites; of Ashbel, the clan of the Ashbelites; of Ahiram, the clan of the Ahiramites;

39of Shephupham, the clan of the Shuphamites; of Hupham, the clan of the Huphamites.

40The sons of Bela were Ard and Naaman: of Ard, the clan of the Ardites; of Naaman, the clan of the Naamites.

41These are the sons of Benjamin by their clans, and those counted of them were forty-five thousand six hundred.

42These are the sons of Dan by their clans: of Shuham, the clan of the Shuhamites. These are the clans of Dan by their clans.

43All the clans of the Shuhamites, as they were counted, were sixty-four thousand four hundred.

44The sons of Asher by their clans: of Imnah, the clan of the Imnites; of Ishvi, the clan of the Ishvites; of Beriah, the clan of the Beriites.

45Of the sons of Beriah: of Heber, the clan of the Heberites; of Malchiel, the clan of the Malchielites.

46The name of Asher's daughter was Serah.

47These are the clans of the sons of Asher as they were counted, fifty-three thousand four hundred.

48The sons of Naphtali by their clans: of Jahzeel, the clan of the Jahzeelites; of Guni, the clan of the Gunites;

49of Jezer, the clan of the Jezerites; of Shillem, the clan of the Shillemites.

50These are the clans of Naphtali by their clans, and those counted of them were forty-five thousand four hundred.

51These are those counted of the sons of Israel: six hundred and one thousand seven hundred and thirty.

Dividing the Land

52The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

53"Among these the land shall be divided as an inheritance, by the number of names.

54To the larger you shall give a larger inheritance, and to the smaller you shall give a smaller inheritance. Each shall be given its inheritance by the number of those counted in it.

55But the land shall be divided by lot. They shall inherit by the names of their fathers' tribes.

56Each inheritance shall be divided by lot, between the larger and the smaller."

The Levites

57These are those counted of the Levites by their clans: of Gershon, the clan of the Gershonites; of Kohath, the clan of the Kohathites; of Merari, the clan of the Merarites.

58These are the clans of Levi: the clan of the Libnites, the clan of the Hebronites, the clan of the Mahlites, the clan of the Mushites, the clan of the Korahites. Kohath fathered Amram.

59The name of Amram's wife was Jochebed daughter of Levi, who was born to Levi in Egypt. She bore to Amram Aaron and Moses and Miriam their sister.

60To Aaron were born Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

61But Nadab and Abihu died when they offered strange fire before the LORD.

62Those counted of them were twenty-three thousand, every male from a month old and up. They were not counted among the sons of Israel, because no inheritance was given to them among the sons of Israel.

Not One Was Left

63These are those counted by Moses and Eleazar the priest, who counted the sons of Israel in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.

64Among them there was not a man of those counted by Moses and Aaron the priest, who counted the sons of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai.

65For the LORD had said of them, "They shall surely die in the wilderness." Not a man of them was left, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

Notes

  • v1 "after the plague" — in the Hebrew these words close chapter 25 (25:19), and the count begins at 26:1. The Greek, like the English, puts them together.

  • v4 "who came out of the land of Egypt" — the sentence has no main verb in the Hebrew: from twenty years old and up, as the LORD commanded Moses, and the sons of Israel who came out of the land of Egypt. It joins the command to the list that follows, and it names this generation, born in the wilderness, by the exodus of their fathers.

  • v10 "they became a warning sign" — le-nes, the word for the pole the bronze serpent was set on (21:8): something set up for everyone to see.

  • vv12–50 the clans and Genesis 46 — the clans are the sons of Jacob's sons, and most names match the list of those who went down to Egypt (Genesis 46:8–27). Some are spelled differently: Nemuel for Jemuel, Zerah for Zohar, Zephon for Ziphion, Ozni for Ezbon, Jashub for Job, Shuham for Hushim, Shephupham and Hupham for Muppim and Huppim. Some are missing: Ohad of Simeon, Ishvah of Asher. Ard and Naaman, sons of Benjamin in Genesis 46:21, are here sons of Bela, and Becher, another son of Benjamin there, is here a clan of Ephraim (v35).

  • v14 "twenty-two thousand two hundred" — Simeon had 59,300 in the first count (1:23). No tribe loses more. Zimri, the man killed with Cozbi at Peor, was chief of a fathers' house of the Simeonites (25:14).

  • v33 "Zelophehad… had no sons, only daughters" — five women, named one by one in a list of men's clans. The next chapter is their case.

  • v46 "Asher's daughter was Serah" — the only daughter of Jacob's sons named in the clan lists, as in Genesis 46:17. She is listed, but no clan is counted from her.

  • v51 "six hundred and one thousand seven hundred and thirty" — the twelve tribal totals add up exactly. The first count was 603,550 (1:46). A whole generation has died and been replaced, and the nation is 1,820 smaller. On thousand, elef, see the note on 1:16.

  • v59 "who was born to Levi in Egypt" — the Hebrew is asher yaldah otah le-Levi, whom she bore to Levi, with no subject for she. The Greek supplies one: who bore these to Levi in Egypt.

  • vv64–65 "not a man of them was left" — the sentence of 14:29–30, carried out: In this wilderness your bodies shall fall… except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

These are the clans of the sons of Ephraim as they were counted, thirty-two thousand five hundred. These are the sons of Joseph by their clans.
The sons of Benjamin by their clans: of Bela, the clan of the Belaites; of Ashbel, the clan of the Ashbelites; of Ahiram, the clan of the Ahiramites;
of Shephupham, the clan of the Shuphamites; of Hupham, the clan of the Huphamites.
The sons of Bela were Ard and Naaman: of Ard, the clan of the Ardites; of Naaman, the clan of the Naamites.
These are the sons of Benjamin by their clans, and those counted of them were forty-five thousand six hundred.
These are the sons of Dan by their clans: of Shuham, the clan of the Shuhamites. These are the clans of Dan by their clans.
All the clans of the Shuhamites, as they were counted, were sixty-four thousand four hundred.
The sons of Asher by their clans: of Imnah, the clan of the Imnites; of Ishvi, the clan of the Ishvites; of Beriah, the clan of the Beriites.
Of the sons of Beriah: of Heber, the clan of the Heberites; of Malchiel, the clan of the Malchielites.
The name of Asher's daughter was Serah.
These are the clans of the sons of Asher as they were counted, fifty-three thousand four hundred.
The sons of Naphtali by their clans: of Jahzeel, the clan of the Jahzeelites; of Guni, the clan of the Gunites;
of Jezer, the clan of the Jezerites; of Shillem, the clan of the Shillemites.
These are the clans of Naphtali by their clans, and those counted of them were forty-five thousand four hundred.
These are those counted of the sons of Israel: six hundred and one thousand seven hundred and thirty.
Dividing the Land
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
"Among these the land shall be divided as an inheritance, by the number of names.
To the larger you shall give a larger inheritance, and to the smaller you shall give a smaller inheritance. Each shall be given its inheritance by the number of those counted in it.
But the land shall be divided by lot. They shall inherit by the names of their fathers' tribes.
Each inheritance shall be divided by lot, between the larger and the smaller."
The Levites
These are those counted of the Levites by their clans: of Gershon, the clan of the Gershonites; of Kohath, the clan of the Kohathites; of Merari, the clan of the Merarites.
These are the clans of Levi: the clan of the Libnites, the clan of the Hebronites, the clan of the Mahlites, the clan of the Mushites, the clan of the Korahites. Kohath fathered Amram.
The name of Amram's wife was Jochebed daughter of Levi, who was born to Levi in Egypt. She bore to Amram Aaron and Moses and Miriam their sister.
To Aaron were born Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
But Nadab and Abihu died when they offered strange fire before the LORD.

Those counted of them were twenty-three thousand, every male from a month old and up. They were not counted among the sons of Israel, because no inheritance was given to them among the sons of Israel.
Not One Was Left
These are those counted by Moses and Eleazar the priest, who counted the sons of Israel in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
Among them there was not a man of those counted by Moses and Aaron the priest, who counted the sons of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai.
For the LORD had said of them, "They shall surely die in the wilderness." Not a man of them was left, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
